summary.text: John Deaton is a Marine Corps veteran and Rhode Island trial attorney who was the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts in 2024, losing to Elizabeth Warren, and won the 2026 Republican nomination unopposed. He describes his campaign as centered on congressional term limits, reducing federal spending and lowering the cost of living.

paragraphs.text: John Deaton attended Highland Park High School, and he has often described a low-income upbringing in a violent, impoverished Highland Park neighborhood of Detroit.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Eastern Michigan University and a J.D. from New England Law in 1995.

Deaton served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1995 to 2002, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as Marine Senior Defense Counsel and Chief Prosecutor at Marine Corps Air Station and as a Special Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Arizona.
He became the owner and managing partner of Deaton Law Firm, and Ballotpedia also describes him as a bestselling author.
Deaton moved from Rhode Island to Massachusetts before his first Senate run, and he lives in Bolton.
Deaton won the Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts in September 2024 and lost the November general election to Warren, 59.8% to 40.0%.
He launched his 2026 campaign on November 10, 2025, challenging Sen. Ed Markey, and won the September 1, 2026 Republican primary unopposed with 99.3% of the vote.

He has signed the U.S. Term Limits Pledge and pledged to serve no more than two six-year terms. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a "U.S. Marine veteran, cancer survivor, father to three daughters, trial attorney, author."
